THE LEXICON OF PLACE is the workspace-wide spatial-vocabulary rename: CellId -> Vertex, RoomAddr -> Facet, RoomId -> FacetId, CellMap -> VertexMap, NearestCellIndex -> NearestVertexIndex, Geosphere::cells() -> vertices(), cell_count() -> vertex_count(), Geosphere::level -> depth, windows/vessel/src/band.rs -> depth.rs. About 16,200 sites across kernel, every domain, every window, cli and clients. Decisions 0246-0247. IT WILL CONFLICT WITH EVERYTHING and Nathans timing call was to land it fast so parallel campaigns absorb it rather than fight it. PRE-FLIGHT DONE, so you know what has and has not been checked: gate-commit green 43.5s; FULL WORKSPACE SUITE RUN LOCALLY, 4269 tests 4269 passed; doctests green; vessel-check world-check game-check all OK; seam-guard 8 sites all GUARDED; rebaseline and rebaseline-goldens both run and ZERO byte-goldens moved; Sluice-Headline trailer verified to RESOLVE via sluice_headline_of before submitting. THE HEADLINE RESULT IS BYTE-IDENTITY: not one seed-42 world, session snapshot, scene, surrounds, locale JSON, almanac or elevation map moved. It did NOT hold by itself and the three catches are the transferable part. ONE: RENDERED PROSE IS A SERIALIZATION BOUNDARY. Sweepers renamed 992 cells to 992 vertices inside almanac output; the almanac ended up saying BOTH words in one sentence. Rendered prose stays cell because a person reads it and vertex is engine vocabulary. TWO: A PREDICATE DESCRIPTION IS SERIALIZED INTO EVERY WORLD. Four moved (cell-id, occ-site, ocean-fraction, highest-elevation-m) and world-seed-42.json grew by exactly the 9 bytes those four account for. Decision 0246 freezes a description the same way it freezes a name. THREE: NOT EVERY BYTE-GOLDEN IS REACHABLE BY A REBASELINE COMMAND. windows/locale/tests/fixtures/column_before.txt is pinned by a test make rebaseline-goldens does not run, so its drift was invisible to every regeneration path and ONLY the full workspace suite caught it. The golden set is larger than the set any rebaseline rewrites - which is why running the full suite locally before submitting is not redundant with the drift check. A FOURTH FINDING THAT COSTS EVERY CAMPAIGN, not just this one: the plans definition-of-done and all six of my dispatch briefs specified a verification grep of backslash-b backslash-w-star [Cc]ell backslash-w-star backslash-b, which CANNOT MATCH ALL-CAPS. About 80 occurrences across five crates (ISLAND_CELL_CAP, MIN_SETTLEABLE_CELLS, GENESIS_TOP_CELLS, LOUD_REACH_CELLS_FLOOR, CONSERVATION_CELLS and others) were invisible to the check meant to PROVE the sweep complete. A sweeper could finish, run the required grep, get a clean residue, and be wrong. Caught by a subagent noticing the asymmetry, not by the check. The general shape worth keeping: a case-sensitive character class is a scope limit you wrote yourself, and enumerating the cases makes the pattern READ as exhaustive. The shipped guard lowercases before comparing so it does not inherit the blind spot. ALSO LANDS a re-accretion guard, cli/tests/suite/lexicon_guard.rs, as a RATCHET rather than an allowlist: about 108 files still hold the word legitimately (a Cell in the chamber lattice, a SurroundsCell in the chart, a markdown-table cell in the trope report), so a gate failing on the words existence would be red on day one and trained away, and an allowlist of type names would pass a NEW vertex-sense local sitting in the same file. It reads docs/audits/lexicon-inventory.tsv and fails on NOVELTY. Proved non-vacuous against a deliberate reintroduction.
